senses.gloss: m. (κάλκανθος, calcanthum) vitriol (also called atramentum sutorum, v. Sm. Ant. s. v.), used as an ingredient of shoe-black, and of ink.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 2:3">Gitt. II, 3</cite> <he>ובקנ׳</he> and with calcanthum (as writing ink); expl.
<cite ref="Eruvin 13a:10-12">Erub. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>דבר אחד</he> … <he>וק׳ שמו וכ׳</he> I have an ingredient whose name is calcanthum, which I put into the ink.

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 11:18">Tosef. Sabb. XI</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 12:18">XII</cite>), 18 <he>אחד נותן את הדיו … הק׳</he> if one puts in the (dry) ink, another the water, and a third person the calcanthum; a. e.
